column2: req_desc

Puzzle grid semantics
The room shows grid "Puzzle grid" whose squares are gridcells with the exact accessible names and data hooks defined in Public screens and controls.

Letter entry and auto-advance
A letter key writes the upper-case letter and moves the cursor by the auto-advance rule in Interactions.

Movement and deletion keys
Arrow keys, Space, Enter, Backspace and Delete behave exactly as the grid keyboard rules in Interactions state, skipping black squares.

Keyboard solving journey
A host solver fills words in a seeded 5x5 game using only the keyboard, and every touched square's name and state are exact, before and after a reload.

Tab between clues
Tab and Shift+Tab move between clues in the published clue order with wrap-around and never take focus out of the grid.

Clue lists and clue bar
The Across and Down clue lists mark the active and crossing clues, and the clue bar shows the active clue in the published format.

Desk and tablet room boards
At 1280x800 and 768x1024 the room arranges the grid, clue tiles and player tiles in the published order and columns, with no horizontal overflow.

Clue navigation journey
A host solver steps through clues by Tab, picks a Down clue by click and leaves the grid with Escape, and the clue marks and clue bar text are exact at each step.

Phone room board
Below 768 px wide the room shows the clue bar, grid, letter keyboard and player tiles in the published order, with the clue lists inert and no horizontal overflow at 375x812.

Letter keyboard and touch selection
On a phone the on-screen letter keyboard enters letters and the touch rules select squares and switch direction, without opening the device keyboard.

Phone solving journey
An invited friend at 375x812 solves by tapping squares, the clue bar buttons and the letter keyboard, with reduced motion on.

Guest players
A visitor becomes a guest player by choosing a display name of 1 to 24 characters and receives the published player cookie.

Share dialog
Share opens dialog "Share game" with the game link and a Copy link control that announces its result.

Joining by link
Anyone with a player cookie who opens an active game link joins that game with the first free colour, as limited by the player cap.

Link turn-off and replacement
The host can turn the game link off or replace it, after which the old link grants nothing, including to live connections already open on it.

Live shared play
Other players' letters, pencil marks, check marks and cursor blocks appear in place within two seconds, with no reload and no movement of the viewer's own cursor.

Shared play journey
Two players join by link, type into one word and see each other live, and then the host turns the link off and the friend's view shows the published sentence.

Server-sequenced writes
Every write to the game gets the next sequence number, and every screen settles on the value with the highest sequence number for each square.

Locked squares
Squares that are checked right or revealed refuse every later write with the published conflict and notice, and keep their value.

Operation replay keys
A write sent again with the same client operation id returns the stored result without a new sequence number, and reusing that id for a different write answers 409.

Live message rate limit
Writes beyond the per-player rate are refused with the published error and notice, as qualified in Business rules.

Same-square journey
Two players write different letters to one square at the same moment, both screens and the stored game agree on the last accepted value, and a write to a revealed square changes nothing.

Check and Reveal menus
Check and Reveal each open a menu of Square, Word and Puzzle that works fully by keyboard and returns focus as published.

Check and reveal rules
Check marks filled unlocked squares wrong or right, reveal writes and locks answers, and both are stored, broadcast and counted as published in Business rules.

Check and reveal journey
A host solver checks a word, reveals a square and checks the puzzle by keyboard, while a friend sees every mark live and both keep them after a reload.

Pencil mode
The period key and the Pencil button toggle pencil mode, whose letters are stored and shown as pencil marks until a pen letter replaces them.

Rebus entry
The Insert key and the Rebus button open an inline rebus editor that commits up to eight letters or digits as one entry.

Open editors survive live updates
Timer ticks and incoming live messages never close an open rebus editor, menu or dialog, clear its draft or move focus.

Pencil and rebus journey
A host solver pencils in letters, overwrites one in pen, commits a STAR rebus, cancels another, and checks, and the stored game keeps the full rebus string.

Server-owned solve timer
The server runs, pauses, resumes and freezes the shared solve time by the presence rules in Business rules, and every screen shows the server's value.

Timer display and personal pause
The room shows the solve time in the published format, and Pause my timer freezes only that viewer's display.

Timer journey
Two players leave, the server pauses the timer at the moment the last one left, and when one returns the timer resumes from that value.

Solve detection
A game becomes solved exactly once, at the write that makes every square match its answer, and then refuses further writes.

Puzzle solved dialog
Every player in the room sees dialog "Puzzle solved" with the published heading and line, focus on its heading, and no motion under reduced motion.

Solved journey
A friend types the last letter, both players see the solved dialog with the same time, the timer freezes, and typing afterwards is refused.

Grid announcements
The polite status "Grid announcements" region announces clue changes, check and reveal results, joins, leaves and the solve with the published copy.

Presence and player tiles
list "Players" shows each player's name, colour and presence, and it updates live as players join and leave.

Announcements journey
A host solver moves, checks and hears a friend join and leave, and every announcement and square name along the way is exact.

Overlap text format
The app parses the Overlap text format deterministically, computes numbering by the published rule, and accepts no other format.

Upload limits and line-numbered errors
Uploads that break a published limit or format rule are refused with the published size answer or line-numbered errors, in the published order.

Upload stored as submitted
A valid upload is stored in object storage byte for byte under the published key, its sha256 is recorded, and Download original returns exactly those bytes.

Private uploads
An uploaded puzzle is visible only to its uploader and to players of games on it, and any other caller gets 404.

Upload journey
A hobby constructor picks a name by keyboard, uploads text with three errors, reads the exact messages, fixes them, and opens a room on the parsed puzzle.

History entries
Each participant of a solved game gets one history entry in list "History", in the published row format, which survives reloads and new browser contexts.

Solve record object
Each solved game has exactly one solve record object at the published key, whose operation log and timer segments equal the game's.

Replay from the solve record
Replay steps through a finished game from its solve record, from step 0 showing the starting grid to the last step showing the final grid, with the published step controls and square hooks.

History journey
Two players solve a game, both see the history row after a reload, the downloaded solve record matches the game, and a player who never joined has no row.

Storage outage behaviour
While object storage is unreachable, the health route, uploads, downloads and solve records behave exactly as published, with the outage copy.

Recovery without restart
When object storage returns, uploads and downloads work again without a restart, and deferred solve records are written exactly once.

Upload outage journey
On the storage-outage instance an upload shows the outage copy, keeps the text and focus in the dialog and creates no puzzle, and the same upload succeeds on the normal instance.

Run manifest, health and config
The app runs from /app/run.json on port 4173, answers the health route, and serves the published config route.

Grading routes
With OVERLAP_GRADING=1 the seed and session routes create players, puzzles and games exactly as published, and without it they do not exist.

Error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the one published body shape and codes, and is chosen by the one published precedence.

Server boundary
The server accepts same-origin requests and live connections only, enforces the published body sizes, and never serves source files or credentials.

Board and filters
The board lists library and own puzzles as tiles with live in-progress counts, and filter chips that live in the URL and update the board in place.

Dialogs, menus and room shortcuts
Every dialog keeps Tab inside itself, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener, and the room shortcuts work from any room control.

Pivot band motion and reduced motion
Switching direction runs the Pivot band shrink-then-grow and the clue scroll in the published phases, and under reduced motion they jump to the same end state at once.

Dense-tiles visual language
Every screen is one fitted tile board in Albert Sans and the paper-grey and brass palette, with no rules, square corners, and brass on exactly one element.

Home hero board
The home page shows the published two-by-two hero board with its dithered grid image and its phone arrangement.

Credentials and bundled assets
Service credentials come only from the environment and never reach the browser, and fonts and icons are served by the app itself.

Solving settings
Settings opens dialog "Solving settings" with three checkboxes that save to the player at once through the settings route and stay after reloads and in new browser contexts.

Settings and the cursor
With Skip filled squares off or Jump to the next clue on, a letter moves the cursor by the published variant of the auto-advance rule, and a refused write moves it the same way.

Autocheck
With Autocheck my letters on, the server checks each of that player's pen entries in the same write and marks it wrong or right as published, while other players' writes stay unchecked.

Autocheck with pencil and rebus
Pencil writes and clears are never autochecked, a committed rebus is autochecked as one whole entry, and autochecked writes leave checked_count unchanged.

Clue references in uploads
Uploaded clue text that refers to a clue the grid does not have, or to starred clues when none is starred, is refused with the published line message in the published checking order.

Linked clues
The room marks the clues and squares linked to the active clue, in both directions of reference, with the published data hooks, and the puzzle JSON lists each clue's links.

Linked clue announcements and Alt+L
A clue change announces the active clue's linked clues in the published sentence, and Alt+L moves to the next linked clue.

Clear word and clear puzzle
Clear word keeps letters that sit in a full crossing word unless nothing else is left to clear, Clear puzzle clears every unlocked square, and both are sequenced, stored and broadcast as published.

Clear menu and confirmation
Clear opens menu "Clear" by button, touch or Alt+X, and Clear puzzle asks in dialog "Clear the puzzle?" before it clears anything.

Race games and teams
A race game is created from the board or the API, every player starts watching, and players choose Team 1, Team 2 or Watch until the host starts the race.

Team grids
In a race each team writes into its own grid, and letters, pencil marks, clears and cursors reach only that team's players.

Claims by check
A racer's check of one square claims it for their team when it is right, writing it into both teams' grids and scoring one point, and marks it wrong only in their own team's grid when it is not.

Race end and result
The race ends at the claim of the last square, and every player sees dialog "Race over" with the published heading and scores.

Race journey
Two players on opposite teams race on one game, each sees only their own team's letters, claims and scores appear live on both screens, and the last claim ends the race for both.

Live clears and autocheck marks
Other players' clears and autochecked marks appear in place within two seconds, with no reload and no movement of the viewer's own cursor.

Replay timeline
The replay dialog has slider "Replay position" whose keys step, jump to the ends, page by ten and skip to the next or previous check, reveal or clear.

Replay op descriptions
status "Replay op" describes the op that produced the current step in the published sentence.

Replay autoplay
Play advances the replay one step per OVERLAP_REPLAY_STEP_MS divided by the chosen speed, on page timers, and stops at the last step.

Builder grid and symmetry
The puzzle builder at /build toggles black squares together with their partners under the chosen symmetry, with the published default and the diagonal limit.

Builder numbering and clues
The builder numbers its grid live by the Overlap rule and shows one clue field per word, keeping a clue's text while its word's start square and direction are unchanged.

Builder problems
list "Grid problems" lists the builder's problems in the published order and copy, and status "Builder status" counts them.

Builder text
Download text gives the exact published Overlap text and file name for the builder's grid and clues.

Builder save
Save to my puzzles sends the builder's text as an upload, and the stored original is byte for byte the downloaded text.

Builder journey
A hobby constructor builds a 5x5 puzzle by keyboard, sees the problems clear one by one, downloads the text and saves it as their own puzzle.

Solve stats
The solved dialog lists each player's letters and reveals in list "Solve stats" by the published counting rule.

Stats in history and records
History entries, history tiles and solve records carry the same per-player stats as the solved dialog.

Builder save during an outage
On the storage-outage instance Save to my puzzles shows the builder outage copy, keeps the whole draft and creates no puzzle.
/app/run.json is valid JSON with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to start the app.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with its licence, plus the bundled Albert Sans font files and their licence.
Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and the bundled fonts are OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres and MinIO: no SQLite, no data files on disk, and no other database, cache, queue or search service.
Served pages load nothing from another host: fonts, scripts, styles, images and icons all come from the app's own origin.
The app is TypeScript for both server and client, with a committed package-lock.json.
The provided development service definitions and their credentials are left unchanged, and the app reads every value from the environment.
